\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سپیده} \fa{دم} (sepide dam)}{سپیده دم (sepide dam)}]{\fa{سپیده} \fa{دم} (sepide dam) — dawn, daybreak}

\label{lesson:FA-C305-sepide-dam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for from then on, then the Persian for recently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سپیده} \fa{دم}}
\textbf{\fa{سپیده} \fa{دم}} (\emph{sepide dam}) — \textquotedblleft{}dawn, daybreak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ما} \fa{سپیده} \fa{دم} \fa{راه} \fa{افتادیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâ sepide dam râh oftâdim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We set off at dawn.
\end{quote}

Literary; in speech \emph{sobh-e zud}. \emph{sepide} \textquotedblleft{}whiteness\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dam} \textquotedblleft{}breath, moment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sepide} \textquotedblleft{}whiteness, the dawn\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB) is built on \emph{sepid} \textquotedblleft{}white\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{dam} here is the Persian word for \textquotedblleft{}breath, moment\textquotedblright{}: the moment of whiteness. EtymDB gives neither a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sepide dam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sepide dam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sepide dam}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for from then on, then the Persian for recently, then say \emph{sepide dam} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بامداد} (bâmdâd)}{بامداد (bâmdâd)}]{\fa{بامداد} (bâmdâd) — early morning, the small hours}

\label{lesson:FA-C305-bamdad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for recently, then the Persian for dawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بامداد}}
\textbf{\fa{بامداد}} (\emph{bâmdâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}early morning, the small hours\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{زلزله} \fa{ساعت} \fa{چهار} \fa{بامداد} \fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتاد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Zelzele sâ'at-e chahâr-e bâmdâd ettefâq oftâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The earthquake happened at four in the morning.
\end{quote}

The news gives night-time hours with \emph{bâmdâd}: \emph{sâ'at-e se-ye bâmdâd} \textquotedblleft{}3 a.m.\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâmdâd} is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{bāmdād}, \textquotedblleft{}dawn, morning\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâmdâd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâmdâd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâmdâd}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for recently, then the Persian for dawn, then say \emph{bâmdâd} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فردای} \fa{آن} \fa{روز} (fardâ-ye ân ruz)}{فردای آن روز (fardâ-ye ân ruz)}]{\fa{فردای} \fa{آن} \fa{روز} (fardâ-ye ân ruz) — the next day, the following day}

\label{lesson:FA-C305-farda-ye-an-ruz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for dawn, then the Persian for early morning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فردای} \fa{آن} \fa{روز}}
\textbf{\fa{فردای} \fa{آن} \fa{روز}} (\emph{fardâ-ye ân ruz}) — \textquotedblleft{}the next day, the following day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فردای} \fa{آن} \fa{روز} \fa{دوباره} \fa{به} \fa{بیمارستان} \fa{رفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Fardâ-ye ân ruz dobâre be bimârestân raftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The next day we went to the hospital again.
\end{quote}

In a story set in the past, \emph{fardâ} alone would mean \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}; this phrase, or \emph{ruz-e ba'd}, gives \textquotedblleft{}the day after\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fardâ} \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}, \emph{ân} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ruz} \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{} are inherited Persian; EtymDB takes \emph{ruz} back through Middle Persian to Old Persian \emph{rauča-}, \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fardâ-ye ân ruz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fardâ-ye ân ruz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fardâ-ye ân ruz}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for dawn, then the Persian for early morning, then say \emph{fardâ-ye ân ruz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هنگام} (hengâm)}{هنگام (hengâm)}]{\fa{هنگام} (hengâm) — the time, the season (formal); at the time of}

\label{lesson:FA-C305-hengam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for early morning, then the Persian for the next day.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هنگام}}
\textbf{\fa{هنگام}} (\emph{hengâm}) — \textquotedblleft{}the time, the season (formal); at the time of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هنگام} \fa{غروب} \fa{به} \fa{ساحل} \fa{رسیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hengâm-e ghorub be sâhel residim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We reached the beach at sunset.
\end{quote}

Formal, with the ezafe: \emph{hengâm-e shâm} \textquotedblleft{}at dinner time\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Hengâmi ke} \textquotedblleft{}when\textquotedblright{} opens a clause.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hengâm} is a native Persian word. EtymDB lists it without a parent, and its deeper origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hengâm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hengâm}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for early morning, then the Persian for the next day, then say \emph{hengâm} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شبانه} \fa{روز} (shabâne ruz)}{شبانه روز (shabâne ruz)}]{\fa{شبانه} \fa{روز} (shabâne ruz) — round the clock, day and night; a full day}

\label{lesson:FA-C305-shabane-ruz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the next day, then the Persian for the time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شبانه} \fa{روز}}
\textbf{\fa{شبانه} \fa{روز}} (\emph{shabâne ruz}) — \textquotedblleft{}round the clock, day and night; a full day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{بیمارستان} \fa{شبانه} \fa{روز} \fa{کار} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U dar bimârestân shabâne ruz kâr mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She worked round the clock at the hospital.
\end{quote}

Also a noun, a full twenty-four hours: \emph{do shabâne ruz} \textquotedblleft{}two days and nights\textquotedblright{}. Built from \emph{shab} \textquotedblleft{}night\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-âne} and \emph{ruz} \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shabâne ruz} joins \emph{shabâne} \textquotedblleft{}nightly\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{shab} \textquotedblleft{}night\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{ruz} \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{}; both are inherited Persian. EtymDB takes \emph{ruz} back through Middle Persian to Old Persian \emph{rauča-}, and sets \emph{shab} beside Sanskrit \emph{kṣap-} \textquotedblleft{}night\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
